title: Hypoxia is a moving front with asymmetric faces
hypothesis: In MC38 tumors, transcriptional hypoxia is organized as a contiguous oxygen front on tissue: velocity-defined entering and exiting cells form opposite faces of an interface, persistent cells occupy an off-ribbon dwell/core, and the front carries a stereotyped immune skirt (CAF/neutrophil enriched, CD8/C1qc depleted). ImageIT/GFP marks hypoxic history, not ongoing transcriptional state. Entry and exit are molecularly asymmetric (ISR/stress entry vs dual OXPHOS+glycolysis exit), contradicting a simple glycolysis↔OXPHOS flip.
predictions: Enter and exit abut spatially more than label shuffle allows
Persist under-occupies the enter×exit ribbon relative to enter/exit
GFP+ gate is not synonymous with persistent hypoxia
Front neighborhoods are CAF/neutrophil-rich and CD8-poor
conclusions_supported: H≤8 MAP overlay removes demux edge artifact and retains 86.7% of cells
Overlay deep→exit enrichment 1.25× (tumor shuffle p≈0.061, z≈1.58)
Front/polarity spatial autocorrelation Morans I ≈0.66/0.64 vs hypoxia_score ≈0.03
Persist on top-20% ribbon 17.6% vs enter 33.3% / exit 35.0%
Entry stress↑ exit metabolic reboot↑ (met_sum p≈4.6e-84)
